_meta.revision: P1 revision: P1-03 score-ratio resolution order (+ config.score_recon_disc_ratio=null caveat), P1-07 training_histories per-training-epoch vs epoch_metrics per-eval-epoch axis distinction, and appended observed anomaly_type_vocabulary per dataset (semanticist request R4).
_meta.purpose: Machine-readable schema sidecar to data-schema.md. file_kind -> fields/dtypes/shapes + dynamic-vs-stable map. Backend may codegen its data-access layer against this.

experiment_dir.children: one subtree per dataset, nested by results_subdir (see dataset_taxonomy)

dataset_dir.note: Leaf training/eval unit. Path = experiment_dir + results_subdir. SWaT is a single training run producing TWO sibling leaf dirs (A1A2_full, A1A2_excl22).

dataset_taxonomy.active_universe_count: 39 (5 base + 28 SMD + 6 Exathlon) per run_base_experiments docstring; current full-rerun queue uses 7 dataset keys
dataset_taxonomy.depth_warning: dataset leaf nesting is 1 OR 2 levels deep (PSM=1, SWaT/A1A2_full=2). Dashboard discovery MUST find leaf dirs by presence of epoch_metrics.json (or experiment_metadata.json) rather than assuming a fixed depth.

epoch_metrics.json.role: Per-eval-epoch performance trend. PRIMARY source for epoch-trend explorer, ranking, GIFs.

epoch_entry.dynamic_note: The ~185 metric keys per entry are the DYNAMIC SURFACE. They may be renamed/added/removed across runs/code versions while {eval_interval, epochs:[...]} and the per-entry 'epoch' field stay stable. NO hard-coded metric list. Discover keys at runtime by union over all entries (some keys appear only after warmup).

scalar_metric_families.point_adjust_sweep: pa_<K>_{f1,precision,recall,roc_auc,prc_auc} for K in {0,5,10,...,100} (21 thresholds x 5 = 105 keys)

nullable_fields._train_feature_disc_mean: null during teacher-only warmup epochs (epoch<=teacher_only_warmup_epochs); array later
nullable_fields.note: JSON literal 'null' appears (~100x in PSM file). Underscore-prefixed keys are internal/diagnostic; UI may hide by default.

experiment_metadata.json.role: Best-epoch snapshot + full config + loss stats + timing + provenance. PRIMARY for config inspector, ranking-by-best, completion marker.

metrics.note: best-epoch metric dict; SAME dynamic key family as epoch_metrics entry (minus _train_* / epoch / timing). For excl22 worker this is the excl22 metrics.

disc_metrics.note: discrepancy-only score variant; same metric key family

teacher_recon_metrics.note: teacher-recon-only score variant; same key family

student_recon_metrics.note: student-recon-only score variant; same key family

config.note: full hyperparameter snapshot; DYNAMIC (config fields evolve). Identical content to best_config.json

conditional_toplevel_fields.metrics_excl_region22: present when excl22 eval ran (any SWaT dir); writer :2131
conditional_toplevel_fields.metrics_full: present only when swat_eval_mode=='excl22'; full-eval reference; writer :2135
conditional_toplevel_fields._prewarmup_backfill: provenance object {applied,date,old_best_epoch,new_best_epoch,new_best_is_prewarmup,stale_best_model_viz,note}; present only on backfilled runs
conditional_toplevel_fields._lambda_recompute: provenance object {applied,date,ratio,fm_in_score,best_epoch,flipped}; present only on lambda-recomputed runs. PROVENANCE ONLY — read by zero live-code paths (scoring.py reads config.score_recon_disc_ratio, NOT this). 'ratio' is a string like '4:1'. THIS is the authoritative source of the applied recon:disc ratio + fm_in_score on backfilled runs where config.score_recon_disc_ratio is null. See score_ratio_resolution below.

score_ratio_resolution._finding: P1-03 (verified). config.score_recon_disc_ratio is JSON null on the canonical 271 run (field added to config.py:223 AFTER these runs trained). The applied ratio lives in _lambda_recompute.ratio.
resolution_order_for_dashboard: 1. experiment_metadata._lambda_recompute.ratio (parse 'R:1' string -> R) and ._lambda_recompute.fm_in_score, when _lambda_recompute is present
score_ratio_resolution.hazard: A score-formula / 'what carries the detector' panel that reads config.score_recon_disc_ratio alone renders None/blank for every backfilled run. Bind to the resolution order; never show a blank ratio.
score_ratio_resolution.fm_in_score_authority: _lambda_recompute.fm_in_score is the per-run authority for whether FM was inside that run's anomaly score (false on the 271 run, matching scoring.py:237 FM-forced-off as of 2026-06-01).

best_config.json.role: Full hyperparameter config of the run (110 keys). Same content as experiment_metadata.config. PRIMARY for config inspector + comparison diff.
best_config.json.dynamic_note: Config field set evolves with code (new ablation flags added/removed). Discover keys at runtime. Notable groups: architecture (d_model,nhead,num_*_layers,patch_size,num_patches,patchify_mode), masking (masking_ratio,mask_after_encoder,force_mask_anomaly), loss/margin (margin_type,lambda_disc,anomaly_loss_weight), grl_* (~15 keys), fm_* (use_feature_matching,fm_loss_weight,fm_distance_metric), scad_* (~14 keys), score (anomaly_score_mode,eval_disc_weight,eval_fm_weight,score_recon_disc_ratio), schedule (num_epochs,warmup_epochs,teacher_only_warmup_epochs,eval_interval), normalize (normalize_mode,minmax_*).

training_histories.json.role: Per-TRAINING-EPOCH training-loss curves (one entry per trained epoch; the only sub-eval-interval signal). Source for loss-component trends, batch profiling, epoch timings.
training_histories.json.toplevel_keys: string repeat-index (e.g. '0'); usually a single key

axis_hazard._finding: P1-07 (verified). training_histories['0'].train_* lists are PER-TRAINING-EPOCH, NOT per-eval-epoch and NOT per-batch.
axis_hazard.granularity: per-training-epoch: each train_* list has length == num_epochs (500 in PSM example); the companion 'epoch' list == [1,2,...,500]. n_batches_per_epoch=8, so it is NOT batch-granular (the review's 'per-batch/step' wording is imprecise).
axis_hazard.distinct_from: epoch_metrics.json::epochs[] is per-EVAL-epoch (length 100 for the same run, epoch in {5,10,...,500}, spacing eval_interval=5).
axis_hazard.rule: Align training_histories to epoch_metrics by the EPOCH NUMBER (the integer in each list), NEVER by list index. The frontend MUST NOT co-plot the two on one shared epoch x-axis (or shared index); render them as separate traces / separate axes. Bind train_* keys via registry key_namespaces.history but keep the per-training-epoch x distinct.

entry_fields._note: each value is a LIST indexed by TRAINING EPOCH (one entry per trained epoch, length == num_epochs). Many keys; lists may be EMPTY for disabled components (e.g. train_scad_* when use_scad=False).

nested_lists.epoch_anomaly_type_scores: list of dicts (may be {} early epochs)
nested_lists.train_feature_recon_mean: list of per-feature arrays (or None early)
nested_lists.epoch_timings: list of per-epoch timing dicts (epoch_total, forward_approx, ...)

training_histories.json.dynamic_note: Key set tracks enabled loss components; UI must handle empty lists and None entries gracefully.

anomaly_type_metrics.json.role: Per-anomaly-type detection breakdown. Source for performance-by-type charts.
anomaly_type_metrics.json.toplevel_keys: anomaly type name (e.g. 'spike', 'attack', dataset-dependent) — DYNAMIC, dataset-specific vocabulary
anomaly_type_metrics.json.dynamic_note: Anomaly-type vocabulary varies per dataset. Observed: simulation emits the 9-type ANOMALY_TYPE_NAMES set (dataset_sliding.py:34); the real-world runs in trash (PSM/SWaT/WaDi) bucket all anomalies under a single 'spike' key, while best_model_detailed.csv uses coarse {normal,attack} names. Discover type keys at runtime; see top-level anomaly_type_vocabulary for the canonical list + display-name seeds (semanticist R4).

batch_profiling.json.role: One-time per-batch GPU timing breakdown. Source for compute-cost panel.
batch_profiling.json.sidecar: batch_profiling.txt = human pretty-print of same data

best_model_detailed.csv.role: Per-WINDOW best-model sample table (sampled, ~20000 rows). Source for per-sample scatter/hardest-samples.
best_model_detailed.csv.note: row count is the SAMPLED window count, not full test length.

best_epoch_train_scores.npz.role: Per-TIMESTEP train-split anomaly scores at best epoch (for train/test score distribution overlay).

fm_error.CONDITIONAL: present only when fm computed (use_feature_matching) at save time

best_epoch_train_scores.npz.absence_note: MISSING for SWaT excl22 dirs and some variants. Treat as optional.

epoch_scores/epoch_<NNN>_scores.npz.role: Per-TIMESTEP test-split scores at each eval epoch. LARGE family (one per eval epoch, ~100 files, ~0.5MB each). Source for distribution-drift GIFs, threshold sweeps.
epoch_scores/epoch_<NNN>_scores.npz.filename: epoch_{ep:03d}_scores.npz; ep is 1-indexed eval epoch (matches epoch_metrics 'epoch')

fm_error.CONDITIONAL: writer :2859 only saved when fm_p is not None AND config.use_feature_matching; ABSENT otherwise

epoch_scores/epoch_<NNN>_scores.npz.count_example: 100 per dataset dir (one per eval epoch, 5..500)

best_model.pt.role: Best-epoch model weights (torch). NOT read by dashboard (no GPU, no model load).
best_model.pt.note: OPAQUE to dashboard; size info only.

checkpoints/{best_checkpoint.pt,latest_c.note: 13 .pt files & ~3.9GB of the 4.1GB experiment footprint are checkpoints. Dashboard must NOT load these; only stat() for size if at all. Only kept for KEEP_CHECKPOINT_DATASETS subset.

summary.json.role: Experiment-ROOT roll-up across all datasets in the run. Source for experiment-level ranking landing page.
summary.json.note: results[].key uses the dataset KEY (e.g. 'SWaT_A1A2','WaDi_A1'), not the leaf subdir. dir is an ABSOLUTE path captured at write time (may be stale if moved to .trash).

monitoring_log.jsonl.role: Append-only training telemetry, one JSON object per line per monitor tick. Source for live progress / health panel.
monitoring_log.jsonl.nullable: latest_eval_epoch/latest_pak_f1/best_pak_f1/best_epoch are null before first eval; values may be JSON null
monitoring_log.jsonl.note: interpretation is a nested object. Lines may contain non-ASCII (Korean) verdict strings. Last line may be partially written during live run -> parse line-by-line, skip undecodable trailing line.

telemetry/{snapshots.csv,plot.png}.role: Fine-grained hardware telemetry time-series. Optional panel.

visualization/epoch_metrics/*.png.role: Pre-rendered per-epoch trend plots. Browseable in viz gallery (the dashboard ALSO re-derives trends from epoch_metrics.json for interactivity/GIFs).
visualization/epoch_metrics/*.png.count_range: 7-9 (excl22 dirs tend to have 7; full dirs 9)

visualization/best_model/*.png.role: Pre-rendered best-model diagnostic plots. Largest gallery.
visualization/best_model/*.png.count_range: 22-23 (PSM 23; SWaT/WaDi 22; excl22 21-22). Set varies with config (FM/GRL/SCAD trends present only when enabled).
visualization/best_model/*.png.stale_marker: STALE_VIZ.txt may be present (plain text) flagging PNGs that no longer match the recomputed best_epoch (2026-06-01 prewarmup backfill). UI should surface this as a caveat badge.

score_variant_blocks.metrics: primary adaptive score (recon + downweighted disc; FM dropped from score as of 2026-06-01)

metric_dictionary.fm_in_score_note: As of 2026-06-01 (mae_anomaly/scoring.py:237,248) FM is EXCLUDED from the anomaly score (scaled_fm always None, fm_active forced False); recon:disc fixed at score_recon_disc_ratio (default 4:1). fm_error arrays/fm_loss STILL recorded as diagnostics. Per-run FM-in-score authority = _lambda_recompute.fm_in_score (false on the 271 run).
metric_dictionary.score_ratio_resolution_note: P1-03: config.score_recon_disc_ratio is null on backfilled runs (field added to config.py:223 after these runs). Resolve the applied recon:disc ratio in this order: (1) experiment_metadata._lambda_recompute.ratio (parse 'R:1' -> R) + .fm_in_score when present; (2) else config.score_recon_disc_ratio when non-null; (3) else 4.0 (scoring.py:247). NEVER read config.score_recon_disc_ratio alone for a score-formula panel or it renders blank. See file_kinds.experiment_metadata.json.score_ratio_resolution.

anomaly_type_vocabulary._purpose: Semanticist request R4: observed anomaly-type key vocabulary per dataset, so the metric registry can seed friendlier display names. The vocabulary is treated as FULLY DYNAMIC otherwise — discover keys at runtime from anomaly_type_metrics.json (and the anomaly_type_name column of best_model_detailed.csv); these are only OBSERVED seeds, not an exhaustive or stable contract.

canonical_full_vocabulary._source: mae_anomaly/dataset_sliding.py:34 ANOMALY_TYPE_NAMES (the simulation/sliding generator's full type set; index 0 = 'normal', 1-9 = anomaly types). evaluator.py:1992-1993 maps integer anomaly_type codes -> these names.

observed_per_dataset._note: Keys ACTUALLY observed in anomaly_type_metrics.json across the .trash/0601/pre_fullrerun complete runs (271/274/286/287). All real-world datasets in these runs bucketed their anomalies under the single type 'spike'. The simulation dataset (not in this trash set) emits all 9 types from canonical_full_vocabulary. best_model_detailed.csv::anomaly_type_name additionally exposes the coarse {normal, attack} labels.

anomaly_type_vocabulary.dashboard_guidance: Render type keys dynamically; look up display_name_seeds for a friendlier label when a key matches, else title-case the raw key and badge it 'inferred name'. Do NOT hard-code the per-dataset key list — a dataset's vocabulary is whatever keys its anomaly_type_metrics.json contains at load time.

STABLE_directory_structure: presence of summary.json + monitoring_log.jsonl at experiment root

dataset leaf dir contains the same FILE KINDS (epoch_metrics.json, experiment_metadata.json, best_config.json, training_histories.json, anomaly_type_metrics.json, batch_profiling.{json,txt}, best_model.pt, best_model_detailed.csv, visualization/{epoch_metrics,best_model}/, checkpoints/, epoch_scores/)
each epoch entry has an integer 'epoch' key
NPZ array names within a file (adaptive_score/teacher_recon_error/discrepancy_error/point_labels [+fm_error])
monitoring_log.jsonl is JSONL (one object per line)
DYNAMIC_contents: the ~185 metric KEYS inside each epoch_metrics epoch entry (renamed/added/removed across code versions)
the ~110 config KEYS in best_config.json / experiment_metadata.config (ablation flags evolve)
the anomaly-type KEYS in anomaly_type_metrics.json (dataset-specific vocabulary)
WHICH visualization PNGs exist (FM/GRL/SCAD trend plots conditional on enabled components)
WHETHER fm_error array exists in an NPZ (conditional on use_feature_matching at save time)
WHETHER conditional metadata blocks exist (metrics_excl_region22, metrics_full, _prewarmup_backfill, _lambda_recompute)
training_histories list keys present/empty (depends on enabled loss components)
dynamic_vs_stable_map.discovery_rule: Backend MUST: (1) discover leaf dataset dirs by presence of epoch_metrics.json/experiment_metadata.json at depth 1-2; (2) build the metric column set by UNION over all epoch entries AND all score-variant blocks at load time; (3) treat every metric key as data-driven; infer direction/family by documented name-pattern fallback (see metric_dictionary), badge inferred ones; (4) never assume a key exists — null/missing must degrade gracefully.

variety_cardinality.dataset_dirs_per_experiment: varies 1..8 (incomplete/aborted runs have fewer; SWaT contributes 2)
variety_cardinality.epochs_per_run: num_epochs 500, eval_interval 5 => 100 eval points => 100 epoch entries + ~100 epoch_scores NPZ
variety_cardinality.swat_dual_eval: SWaT/A1A2_full and SWaT/A1A2_excl22 are siblings; excl22 lacks best_epoch_train_scores.npz; metadata carries metrics_full/metrics_excl_region22 cross-refs
variety_cardinality.schema_drift: Live run dataset dirs and trash 271 share IDENTICAL epoch_metrics schema (185 keys). Drift dimension is over TIME/code-version, not within this snapshot. Older archived runs (outside this trash set) may have different/fewer metric keys -> dynamic discovery required.

edge_cases_hazards.in_progress_dataset_dir: Live leaf dir may have ONLY checkpoints/ + epoch_scores/ (no epoch_metrics.json/experiment_metadata.json/best_model yet). Treat experiment_metadata.json as the completion marker (writer uses it as skip-marker :2298).
edge_cases_hazards.append_during_read: monitoring_log.jsonl AND epoch_scores/ are actively appended by the live run. Read JSONL line-by-line tolerating a truncated final line; list-then-load NPZ to avoid racing a half-written file (catch zipfile.BadZipFile / EOFError and skip).
edge_cases_hazards.missing_best_model: best_epoch_train_scores.npz absent for excl22 and some variants; best_model.pt may be absent mid-run. Guard all reads.
edge_cases_hazards.null_in_json: epoch_metrics has JSON null for _train_feature_disc_* during warmup; monitoring_log has null pre-eval fields. JSON may (rarely) contain NaN/Infinity literals from default=float dumps -> use a tolerant JSON parser or sanitize.
edge_cases_hazards.large_npz_lazy: epoch_scores has ~100 NPZ/dir; per-timestep arrays up to ~176K float32. Load lazily/on-demand, never eager-load all into memory; downsample for plotting.
edge_cases_hazards.stale_viz_marker: STALE_VIZ.txt flags PNGs inconsistent with recomputed best_epoch. Surface as caveat, do not trust those PNGs as ground truth.
edge_cases_hazards.absolute_paths_in_summary: summary.json results[].dir are absolute paths captured at run time; do not rely on them after a dir is moved (e.g. to .trash). Resolve relative to the experiment dir instead.
edge_cases_hazards.png_count_variance: 22-23 best_model + 7-9 epoch_metrics PNGs; gallery must enumerate dynamically, not assume a fixed list.
edge_cases_hazards.non_ascii: monitoring_log judgment strings contain Korean; read as UTF-8.
edge_cases_hazards.depth_ambiguity: leaf dir depth is 1 (PSM) or 2 (SWaT/A1A2_full); discovery must not hard-code depth.
